title: 1952 AHSME Problem 34
statement: The price of an article was increased \(p\%.\) Later the new price was decreased \(p\%.\) If the last price was one dollar, the original price was:

solutions.text:
If the original price is \(P\) dollars, then after both changes its price is \[ \begin{aligned} &P\left(1+\frac p{100}\right) \left(1-\frac p{100}\right)\\ &\qquad=P\left(1-\frac{p^2}{10{,}000}\right). \end{aligned} \] Setting this equal to \(1\) gives \[ P=\frac{10{,}000}{10{,}000-p^2}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Represent the increase and decrease by multiplicative factors
If the original price is \(P,\) then \(P(1+\frac{p}{100})(1-\frac{p}{100})=1\)
